certificationUse.text: The certification mark, as intended to be used by persons authorized by the certifier, certifies that the services are provided by persons who have attained a specific level of education, training, and experience in the field of providing assistance as intervenors to deafblind individuals in their daily living activities and communications. Persons certified as intervenors must possess the requisite knowledge to provide auditory, visual and tactile information to someone who is deafblind for the purposes of assisting the individual who is deafblind to communicate. Intervenors are required to develop knowledge of deafblindness, its history, causes and psychosocial implications, as well as the ethical code governing their services as an intervenors. Intervenors must be proficient in the languages used by the deafblind individuals who they assist and become knowledgeable about the various technical and augmentatives devices available to individuals who are deafblind. A copy of the complete details of the standard are enclosed with this application and accessible to the public in the records of the Canadian Intellectual Property Office.
